update.title: Rebuilt Screenshot Tool as a persistent capture service
update.summary: Replaced per-hotkey application startup with a persistent GTK4 service, then added precise frozen-region selection and exact identity matching for same-titled windows.
update.previewAlt: Screenshot Tool frozen-region selector with live dimensions, keyboard guidance, crosshairs, and a magnified pointer view

blocks.body:
## Keep capture ready between hotkeys

I replaced the one-process-per-hotkey interactive path with a GTK4 service that stays available on the session bus. The `screenshot` command became a thin client: it sends an explicit request while the service moves through idle, freezing, selecting, and saving states. Fullscreen, fixed-region, and named-window capture remained scriptable through the same command.

The service captures a cursor-free desktop frame before opening the selector. It creates the overlay only for the active request and destroys it after saving or cancellation. Pressing the hotkey again while the service is freezing or selecting saves the already frozen frame fullscreen instead of starting competing work. Cancellation clears the request and returns the service to idle.

## Select the exact window and pixels

I joined Wayfire's window geometry to the capture backend through the standard opaque foreign-toplevel identifier. App IDs and titles remained useful labels, but they were no longer identity fallbacks. Two windows with the same title therefore remained distinct, while a window without an exact match stayed visible but could not be captured by guesswork.

Region selection gained live dimensions, one-pixel keyboard movement, a crosshair, and an enlarged eight-times magnifier. Because the selector displays a frozen frame rather than the changing desktop, its target cannot move beneath the pointer.

blocks.alt: Screenshot Tool's frozen selector over an abstract landscape, with a cyan 1038 by 814 selection box, keyboard guidance, crosshairs, and a circular magnifier
blocks.caption: The request-scoped selector kept the desktop frozen while showing live region dimensions, keyboard guidance, and a magnified crosshair.

blocks.body:
## Separate capture from output

I removed the package's embedded protocol client and native capture helper and consumed the versioned `wayland-capture/frame@1` raw-frame contract instead. The service validates the frame and output layout before using the pixels. Regions are cropped from the frozen frame; selected windows receive a fresh capture through their exact identifier after the overlay closes.

Both paths then use the same output layer for atomic file saving, clipboard format, notifications, structured JSON, sound, and optional post-save hooks. That preserved the output boundary established by the earlier Screenshot Tool version while replacing its per-invocation coordination.

blocks.caption: The service persists across requests; the frozen selector exists only for the active request, and exact window capture remains distinct from region cropping.
blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as CLI or hotkey
  participant S as Persistent GTK service
  participant W as Wayland capture boundary
  participant O as Request-scoped selector
  C->>S: Explicit capture request
  S->>W: Capture cursor-free desktop
  W-->>S: Frozen raw frame and output layout
  S->>S: Join window geometry by opaque identity
  S->>O: Create selector for this request
  O-->>S: Region, fullscreen, or exact window
  alt Region or fullscreen
    S->>S: Crop or reuse the frozen frame
  else Exact window
    S->>W: Capture selected opaque identity
    W-->>S: Exact window frame
  end
  S->>S: Apply shared output policy
  S-->>C: File and structured output result

blocks.caption: Service lifecycle ran through its public command and passed its retained package suite.
